profile.reading:
This building, VA11, was the first data center built on Vantage's Ashburn I campus at 45200 Vantage Data Plaza, Sterling, VA 20166; Vantage's own press release announcing the second building, VA12, states VA11's capacity as 30 megawatts, though VA11 has no standalone facility page of its own. Vantage's current campus page describes Ashburn I as 52 acres with six data centers totaling 1.7 million square feet at full buildout and 206 megawatts of critical IT load, a building count matching the VA11 through VA16 numbering tracked in this registry, though Vantage does not explicitly confirm on its own site that all six numbered buildings sit on this specific campus; that campus assignment is inferred from the matching building count rather than independently confirmed.

Vantage is a private, Denver, Colorado-headquartered operator; DigitalBridge acquired the company in March 2017, and in January 2024 Vantage announced a $6.4 billion equity investment round led by DigitalBridge and Silver Lake. Virginia's data center boom is reshaping statewide electricity rates directly relevant to every Ashburn-area facility: in November 2026, the Virginia State Corporation Commission approved new Dominion Energy rates raising a typical residential bill by about $16 a month to roughly $165, while creating a new GS-5 data center rate class effective January 1, 2027, under which facilities with 25 megawatts or more of demand, a threshold VA11 exceeds on its own, face 14-year mandatory contracts and minimum cost-coverage requirements, per Inside Climate News.

Northern Virginia's Loudoun and Prince William counties together form the largest data center market in the world by capacity, and local zoning debate has intensified in recent years as residents, county supervisors, and Dominion Energy weigh the tradeoff between substantial commercial tax revenue from facilities like this one and rising transmission-line construction, land consumption, and residential electricity-rate pressure tied to data center growth. Dominion Energy's long-range integrated resource plans have repeatedly cited Loudoun and Prince William data center demand as the single largest driver of the utility's near-term generation and transmission capital spending, a dynamic that has also drawn scrutiny from the Virginia State Corporation Commission in periodic rate cases. Vantage's Virginia cluster sits among the densest concentration of competing operators anywhere in the world, including Amazon Web Services, Equinix, Digital Realty, and QTS facilities within a few miles.

reading.body:
The Vantage Ashburn I campus in Sterling spans 52 acres and 1.7 million square feet across six buildings, of which VA11 is the first phase, delivered in February 2019. The operator publishes 206 MW of critical IT load for the campus at full buildout and densities up to 300 W per square foot, though the individual capacity of VA11 itself is not separately disclosed. If the 206 MW campus total distributes evenly across six buildings, this would imply roughly 34 MW per building as a working assumption, though the operator does not state this figure.

VA11's completion in early 2019 makes it among the earliest hyperscale facilities in the region, preceding the recent wave of AI-driven data center development in Northern Virginia. The campus sits in a state with 326 mapped facilities but only 23 with published capacity, suggesting most of Virginia's data center footprint operates without disclosed power figures. At 206 MW published capacity across the full Ashburn I campus, this facility ranks outside the top 23 largest published sites in Virginia by individual capacity, falling to rank 24 statewide, and accounts for roughly 15 percent of Virginia's total published 1,375 MW.

The 300 W per square foot density ceiling published for the campus indicates readiness for high-intensity compute workloads, though certification details are not disclosed in the operator's published specifications. Whether VA11 or the broader Ashburn I campus currently operates at design capacity, and what share of the 206 MW is energized today, are not published and cannot be derived from available data.
